# HTTP contract fixtures

Generated by `./scripts/capture_contract.sh` against the frozen Go baseline
`go-baseline-2026-11` (`1f3a87f`) and committed. The capture was run twice in
a row and `diff -r` was clean, so the fixtures are reproducible.

- 172 HTTP cases
- 8 decoded email fixtures
- 13 notes (Redis state, TTS upstream requests, ids, time-format samples)

## Layout

```
cases/NNN_<name>.json     one request/response record
emails/NNN_<name>.email.json decoded MailHog message (subject/body normalized)
notes/NNN_<name>.note.json   Redis snapshots / TTS upstream requests / ids
index.json                ordered list of every fixture
```

## Case shape

```json
{
  "name": "posts_default",
  "request": {
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/api/posts",
    "headers": {"X-Forwarded-For": "203.0.113.10"}
  },
  "response": {
    "status": 200,
    "headers": {"content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
    "json": {"list": [], "total": 0, "page": 1}
  }
}
```

Binary responses use `body_base64` + `body_sha256` + `body_bytes`; text
responses use `text`; empty bodies use `"empty": true`.

## Normalization

- `created_at` / `updated_at` / `deleted_at` → `<timestamp>`
- JWT (`eyJ...`) → `<jwt>`
- 32-char hex unsubscribe token → `<token>`
- 8-char hex random slug (only under key `slug`) → `<random-slug>`
- 6-digit verification codes in emails and login request bodies → `<code>`
- email bodies are quoted-printable-decoded before normalization
- `content-length` is **not** captured (derived from volatile timestamp lengths);
  binary sizes are recorded as `body_bytes`

`index.json.meta` records the Go commit/tag and SHA-256 of the schema/seed.

## Rules

- Do not hand-edit fixtures. Regenerate from the tagged Go baseline.
- A diff means either the Go baseline changed (expected only with a new tag) or
  the capture harness changed. Review both before committing.
- Tests should compare status, headers in the fixture, and normalized JSON.
  Volatile values are already replaced.
